## Teaching points

1. Early IV antibiotic prophylaxis, sterile coverage, tetanus assessment and urgent orthopedic care are priorities in an open fracture.
2. The wound communicates with the fracture even if the skin opening is small.
3. Give prompt IV prophylaxis using the local open-fracture pathway, protect the wound and obtain urgent orthopedic care.
4. Reassess distal circulation and sensation after alignment/support. Tetanus prophylaxis depends on wound type and immunization history.
